projects.projectName: Premera Blue Cross - Producer Portal Development - Phase 1

riskDescription.context: All seven SOW milestones show 'Yet to Start' status with no actual start or end dates recorded, despite the project being in Build + SIT stage and four milestones having passed their scheduled end dates by 2 to 3 months (Design Phase: March 31, Sprint 1-2: April 30, Sprint 3-4: May 31, Development & Testing: June 15). (EMS - Milestones)
riskDescription.condition: If milestone tracking continues to lag actual project progress through the UAT and Go-Live phases.
riskDescription.consequence: Stakeholders may lack visibility into true schedule status, preventing timely intervention if Go-Live (July 1-15) or Hypercare (July 16-August 31) milestones slip, and governance decisions may be made on outdated information.

risks.mitigationPreventiveAction: Implement weekly milestone status review with Engineering Manager to update actual start and end dates by July 5.
risks.contingencyCorrectiveAction: Upon detection of milestone data lag exceeding one week, escalate to project governance board and conduct emergency status reconciliation within 48 hours.

riskDescription.context: Actual effort delivered is 8.0 story points against a baseline of 45.0 (82% below target), and the team record was created on May 22, 2026, which is 2.5 months after the project start date of March 1, 2026. (EMS - Resources, Project Details)
riskDescription.condition: If effort delivery remains well below baseline as sprint work ramps up toward the Development and Testing completion target of June 15.
riskDescription.consequence: Sprint velocity may fall short of what is needed to complete remaining development and testing work, causing the June 15 milestone to slip and compressing the 15-day UAT window that follows.

risks.mitigationPreventiveAction: Conduct capacity analysis and identify senior backup resources to augment team velocity by 30% before June 20 UAT start.
risks.contingencyCorrectiveAction: Once velocity shortfall exceeds 20% for two consecutive sprints, activate backup resources from enterprise pool and escalate to delivery leadership within 24 hours.

riskDescription.context: The project has absorbed 14 scope changes (equivalent to 0.75-1 sprint of additional effort), averaging 3.5 changes per month from March through June, and an open risk signals that further scope additions are likely. (EMS - Risks)
riskDescription.condition: If additional scope changes are accepted without formal impact assessment and change control approval.
riskDescription.consequence: The team may absorb another 0.5 to 0.75 sprint of unplanned effort by project end in December, further compressing the Hypercare phase and increasing the risk of SOW term overrun beyond November 30.

risks.mitigationPreventiveAction: Establish formal change control board with documented approval process and impact assessment for all scope additions by July 10.
risks.contingencyCorrectiveAction: Should scope changes exceed five additional requests after July, invoke scope freeze and communicate revised timeline to client stakeholders.

riskDescription.context: Four major milestones (Design Phase, Sprint 1-2, Sprint 3-4, Development & Testing) have passed their scheduled end dates by 1 to 3 months with no actual completion recorded, and effort delivery is 82% below baseline. (EMS - Milestones, Resources)
riskDescription.condition: If the milestone slippage is real and not solely a data lag issue.
riskDescription.consequence: The project may be 2 to 3 months behind schedule, which would push UAT, Go-Live, and Hypercare milestones into September or October, breaching the SOW end date of November 30.

risks.mitigationPreventiveAction: Conduct immediate schedule reconciliation and rebaseline impacted milestones with client approval by July 8 to establish recovery trajectory.
risks.contingencyCorrectiveAction: Upon confirmation of two-month or greater slippage, activate fast-track plan with parallel UAT and development activities and escalate SOW amendment request to client within 72 hours.

riskDescription.context: The UAT milestone is scheduled for a 15-day window (June 16-30) and starts the day after Development and Testing is scheduled to end (June 15), with no buffer between the two phases. (EMS - Milestones)
riskDescription.condition: If Development and Testing finishes late or requires rework due to quality issues.
riskDescription.consequence: The 15-day UAT window may not be sufficient for client sign-off, which could delay the Go-Live milestone scheduled for July 1-15.

risks.mitigationPreventiveAction: Schedule detailed UAT strategy review with QE leadership by June 25 to validate test coverage and sign-off criteria.
risks.contingencyCorrectiveAction: Once UAT completion risk is identified, implement phased go-live approach with critical functionality first and escalate revised timeline to project board within 48 hours.

riskDescription.context: The Go-Live milestone is scheduled for July 1-15 (15 days), and it depends on UAT completion and sign-off by June 30, but four upstream milestones have passed their scheduled dates with no completion recorded. (EMS - Milestones)
riskDescription.condition: If UAT is delayed or incomplete by June 30 due to upstream slippage.
riskDescription.consequence: Go-Live may be delayed beyond July 15, compressing the 47-day Hypercare phase (July 16-August 31) and increasing the risk of breaching the SOW end date of November 30.

risks.mitigationPreventiveAction: Define explicit go-live readiness criteria and conduct checkpoint review with client stakeholders by June 28 to validate UAT sign-off path.
risks.contingencyCorrectiveAction: Upon UAT delay beyond July 5, activate deferred delivery plan for non-critical features and escalate revised go-live date to executive leadership within 24 hours.

riskDescription.context: The SOW term ends on November 30, 2026, and the Hypercare phase is scheduled to end on August 31, 2026, but four milestones have passed their scheduled dates with no completion recorded, suggesting a 2-3 month delay. (EMS - Milestones, Project Details)
riskDescription.condition: If milestone slippage persists and Hypercare extends beyond August 31 due to upstream delays.
riskDescription.consequence: The project may require effort beyond the SOW end date of November 30, creating an SOW term overrun with potential financial and contractual implications.

risks.mitigationPreventiveAction: Review SOW exit criteria and establish formal sign-off checkpoints with client by July 15 to prevent scope extension.
risks.contingencyCorrectiveAction: Should project timeline extend beyond October 31, initiate formal change request for SOW amendment and communicate commercial impact to client leadership.

riskDescription.context: The Business Analyst role is marked as 'NA' (not available), and the project has absorbed 14 scope changes averaging 3.5 per month with an active scope-change risk signaling more are likely. (EMS - Resources, Risks)
riskDescription.condition: If scope changes continue to be managed without a dedicated Business Analyst through the UAT and Go-Live phases.
riskDescription.consequence: Requirements may be misunderstood or poorly documented, increasing the risk of rework during UAT and delaying client sign-off needed for Go-Live.

risks.mitigationPreventiveAction: Assign interim Business Analyst from enterprise pool or cross-train existing team member for requirement management by July 8.
risks.contingencyCorrectiveAction: When requirement clarification delays exceed three business days, engage senior architect for direct client communication and document decisions immediately.

riskDescription.context: The Engineering Manager (Saitej Ballav) is the sole identified project owner and owns all three documented risks, and no Delivery Manager, QA Manager, or Client Manager is assigned. (EMS - Project Details, Risks)
riskDescription.condition: If the Engineering Manager becomes unavailable or overloaded during critical phases such as UAT or Go-Live.
riskDescription.consequence: Risk management, client escalation, and delivery decisions may be delayed, increasing the likelihood of missed milestones or unresolved issues during Go-Live.

risks.mitigationPreventiveAction: Identify backup senior resource and document RACI matrix with distributed risk ownership across team leads by July 12.
risks.contingencyCorrectiveAction: Backup resource to assume delivery coordination immediately if Engineering Manager is unavailable for more than two consecutive business days.

riskDescription.context: The project is classified as Category 1 (total score 20) with Infrastructure identified as the bottleneck, and all four dimension scores (Infrastructure, Knowledge, Process, Governance) are at the lowest level of 1. (EMS - Project Categorization)
riskDescription.condition: If the Infrastructure bottleneck persists despite the resolution of Data Hub API dependencies on June 29.
riskDescription.consequence: Delivery velocity may remain constrained, preventing the team from recovering the 82% effort shortfall and increasing the risk of missing the Go-Live milestone in July.

risks.mitigationPreventiveAction: Monitor sprint velocity for two sprints post-API resolution and implement infrastructure automation to improve environment stability by July 20.
risks.contingencyCorrectiveAction: Should velocity remain below 70% of baseline after two sprints, engage infrastructure support team and implement parallel development workaround.

riskDescription.context: No finance data is available (planned vs. actual costs, margin, billing, revenue, forecast), and the project has absorbed 14 scope changes equivalent to 0.75-1 sprint of additional effort. (EMS - Finance, Risks)
riskDescription.condition: If the 14 scope changes and any future scope additions are not tracked for cost impact.
riskDescription.consequence: Margin erosion or cost overruns may go undetected, preventing timely corrective action and potentially leading to financial loss or client disputes at project closure.

risks.mitigationPreventiveAction: Implement weekly cost tracking against SOW budget and document financial impact of all scope changes by July 10.
risks.contingencyCorrectiveAction: When cost variance exceeds 15% of SOW budget, initiate formal change request for additional funding and communicate margin impact to finance leadership.

riskDescription.context: RAG status is 'Not Set' across all seven dimensions (Overall, Scope, Cost, Timeline, Quality, Talent, CSAT), and the Go-Green Plan field is empty. (EMS - RAG)
riskDescription.condition: If RAG assessment is not established before the UAT and Go-Live phases begin.
riskDescription.consequence: Stakeholders may lack early warning of deteriorating health in scope, cost, or timeline, preventing timely escalation and intervention if issues arise during UAT or Go-Live.

risks.mitigationPreventiveAction: Establish weekly RAG assessment across all seven dimensions with documented reason and action plans by July 5.
risks.contingencyCorrectiveAction: Upon identification of Red RAG in any dimension, activate immediate recovery plan and escalate to project governance board within 24 hours with mitigation timeline.
